title: Design for Bridge Maintenance Repairs, Region 11
short_description: Engineering design services for standby bridge maintenance repairs across NYSDOT Region 11.
project_location: Albany, New York, USA; Region 11 Wide (NYC)
project_scope: Standby where-and-when bridge maintenance repair design services for NYSDOT Region 11 (New York City area). The tender indicates a region-wide bridge repair program rather than a single defined structure; no bridge count, spans, structural types, or exact intervention measures are specified in the source. Total construction cost is stated as 25 million USD.
services: Design services for bridge maintenance repairs, including structural engineering, civil engineering, utility engineering, traffic design engineering, transportation planning, geotechnical engineering, and construction/project management.
relevance_explanation:
- Bridge-related assignment in a core sbp field.
- Includes structural engineering and design services, not only construction.
- Maintenance/repair of bridges can be relevant, especially for larger bridge rehabilitation programs.
- Region-wide standby/where-and-when format reduces clarity on structural ambition and specific opportunities.
- Presence of broad multidisciplinary scope suggests engineering-led framework-type support rather than a single iconic structure.
- Not a framework agreement for multiple bridges explicitly, but the standby region-wide nature lowers strategic fit compared with a defined complex bridge project.
fee_explanation: No explicit design fee is stated. Available fee-related inputs: engineering design services for a bridge maintenance repair program with total construction cost of 25,000,000 USD, 30-month duration, and multidisciplinary scope including structural, civil, geotechnical, traffic, and utility engineering plus construction/project management.
references_qualifications: No specific reference requirements are stated in the source. Requested disciplines include utility engineering, traffic design engineering, transportation planning, civil engineering, geotechnical engineering, construction/project management, and structural engineering.
